terms.gloss: set up, establish (a custom, a practice, a school)
terms.grammar: verb, third conjugation; with an accusative, or an infinitive (to make a practice of doing)
evidence: Quint. 1.8.5: optimē īnstitūtum est, ut ab Homērō atque Vergiliō lēctiō inciperet
Liv. 5.27.2: cum in pāce īnstituisset puerōs ante urbem lūsūs exercendīque causā prōdūcere
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: “to set up, erect, plant, establish, arrange”; an established practice is īnstitūtum (see practice, custom). Also to train or educate a child (Traupman 29). That something is an established fact is cōnstat (Liv. 3.26.9: id quod cōnstat).

terms.gloss: establish, settle, fix (a state, laws, a date)
evidence: Ov. F. 1.27–28: in annō cōnstituit mēnsēs quīnque bis esse suō
Verg. A. 1.33: tantae mōlis erat Rōmānam condere gentem

phrases.latin: optimē īnstitūtum est, ut ab Homērō atque Vergiliō lēctiō inciperet
phrases.english: It is an excellent established custom that reading should begin with Homer and Vergil.

phrases.latin: tantae mōlis erat Rōmānam condere gentem
phrases.english: So great a task it was to found the Roman people.

phrases.latin: tempora dīgereret cum conditor urbis, in annō cōnstituit mēnsēs quīnque bis esse suō
phrases.english: When the founder of the city was setting the calendar in order, he established that his year should have twice five months.

sources: Lewis & Short: instituo · Lewis & Short: constituo · Lewis & Short: condo
